title: Tracxn's revenue remains flat at Rs 21.3 Cr in Q2 FY27; losses narrow 25.7%
summary:
Data intelligence platform Tracxn announced its Q2 FY27 results, reporting largely flat revenue during the quarter, while its losses narrowed year-on-year.
Tracxn's revenue from operations increased marginally by 0.2% to Rs 21.30 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21.25 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).




Tracxn derives its operating revenue from subscription sales, which provide access to its data and software. However, the company did not disclose a detailed revenue breakup for the quarter.
The company also earned Rs 1.38 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 22.70 crore in Q2 FY27.
Employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost head, increasing 22.5% to Rs 23.33 crore and accounting for 85.4% of the overall expenditure during the quarter. Depreciation expenses stood at Rs 7.5 lakh, compared to Rs 4 lakh in Q2 FY26. Other expenses increased 41% to Rs 3.92 crore.

The company's total expenses rose 25% to Rs 27.32 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21.86 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Despite the increase in expenses, Tracxn narrowed its net loss by 25.7% to Rs 4.13 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to a loss of Rs 5.56 crore in Q2 FY26.
On a half-yearly basis, Tracxn's revenue from operations remained largely flat at Rs 42.38 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 42.44 crore in H1 FY26. However, its net loss widened 60.8% to Rs 7.14 crore during the first half of FY27.

At the close of trading on Wednesday, Tracxn’s shares settled at Rs 32.08, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately Rs 331 crore.

title: PhysicsWallah revenue rises 18% to Rs 1,242 Cr in Q2 FY27; profit jumps 2.1X
summary:
Edtech company PhysicsWallah reported an 18.2% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in Q2 FY27, while its net profit more than doubled during the quarter.

PhysicsWallah’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 1,242 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,051 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statement sourced from NSE.


In terms of revenue mix, the online segment remained the largest contributor, accounting for 55.84% of PhysicsWallah’s operating revenue at Rs 693.5 crore, up 26.3% year-on-year. The offline segment contributed 43.56%, with revenue rising 9.1% to Rs 541 crore, while other operating revenue at Rs 8 crore.

The company also earned Rs 93 crore from other sources, taking its total income to Rs 1,335 crore in Q2 FY27.

On the expense side, employee benefits remained the largest cost component at Rs 522 crore, up 10.4% year-on-year from Rs 473 crore while Cost of materials consumed increased 22.6% to Rs 195 crore from Rs 159 crore.
Depreciation expenses rose 7.6% to Rs 113 crore, while finance costs increased 4% to Rs 26 crore. Other expenses grew 4.6% to Rs 249 crore from Rs 238 crore. Overall expenses increased 10.5% to Rs 1,105 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,000 crore in Q2 FY26.

The Noida-based company’s net profit surged 2.1X year-on-year to Rs 144 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 70 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On a half-yearly basis, the company's revenue from operations increased 20.8% to Rs 2,293 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 1,898 crore in H1 FY26. The company reported a net profit of Rs 55.35 crore in H1 FY27, against a net loss of Rs 57.30 crore in H1 FY26.

At the end of today’s trading session, the Noida-based company’s share price closed at Rs 127.41, giving it a market capitalisation of Rs 37,376 crore

India’s egg market is gradually moving towards organised players, with growing consumer interest in branded products, better quality standards and traceability. This shift has opened up opportunities for companies such as Eggoz, which has built its business around sourcing eggs from farmers and supplying them through an organised distribution network.
`The company continued to expand its business in the fiscal year ended March 2026, with revenue growing 39% year-on-year. However, higher employee and advertising costs weighed on its bottom line, which pushed its losses by 83% during the fiscal year.

Gurugram-based Eggoz’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 180 crore in FY26 from Rs 130 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC),

Founded in 2017 in Bihar by Abhishek Negi and Aditya Singh, Eggoz is operated by Nupa Technologies and follows an asset-light, farmer-led supply chain model. The company works with local poultry farmers to improve egg production, collection and distribution through technology, ensuring fresh eggs reach retailers within 24 hours. It focuses on maintaining quality and freshness while helping farmers access better technology and wider markets
Egg sales remained the company's primary revenue contributor in FY26. Eggoz also earned around Rs 6 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 186 crore during the fiscal year.

Employee benefit expenses increased 50% to Rs 30.8 crore during FY26 from Rs 20.5 crore in FY25. Advertising and promotional expenses saw a sharper jump of 2.9X to Rs 30 crore from Rs 10.5 crore in the previous fiscal.
Transportation costs also rose 32.2% to Rs 7.8 crore, while other expenses such as legal & professional, travelling, collectively added around Rs 17 crore to the total cost.
Consequently, Eggoz's total expenditure increased 48.% year-on-year to Rs 228 crore in FY26 from Rs 154 crore in FY25.

title: Fintech infra startup OneStack raises Rs 12.5 Cr from Shepherd's Hill, others
summary:
Fintech infrastructure startup OneStack has raised Rs 12.5 crore from new investor Shepherd's Hill and existing backers Pentathlon Ventures and AVNM Ventures.
The Mumbai-based startup had previously raised  $2 million in a Series A round in March 2025, led by Pentathlon Ventures, with participation from Yatra Angel Network and existing investors 100Unicorns and Venture Catalysts. With this round, OneStack has raised Rs 45 crore across four funding rounds.
The proceeds will be used to expand its presence among cooperative banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), alongside product development in payments, core banking and regulatory compliance, the company said in a press release.
Founded by Amit Kapoor in 2019, OneStack provides technology infrastructure that enables smaller financial institutions to offer digital banking services without building their own systems. Its platform includes mobile banking, UPI issuing and merchant acquiring, QR payments, debit card management and its OneCBS core banking system.
The company said cooperative banks using its platform can now operate as UPI issuers and acquirers directly with the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), under their own bank handles. This enables them to issue UPI IDs to customers, onboard merchants and settle payments through their own payment rails, while retaining customer relationships, transaction data and merchant discount rate (MDR) revenue.
OneStack plans to extend its platform to NBFCs with tools for customer verification and fraud reporting. Its compliance suite includes integration with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). The company is also an Aadhaar OVSE technology service provider, has integrated eKYC Setu and holds RuPay debit card issuance certification and SU3J licenses under credit bureaus.
OneStack has also partnered with a large private sector bank that sponsors more than 250 cooperative banks. The partnership will provide a route to offer UPI issuing, merchant acquiring and its wider banking platform across the network.
The company claims to serve more than 200 banks across India, including state cooperative banks, district central cooperative banks (DCCBs) and non-scheduled urban cooperative banks (NSUCBs).
India's cooperative banking network presents a sizable market for technology providers. NABARD's 2024-25 annual report records 34 state cooperative banks and 351 DCCBs, which together operated nearly 15,900 branches as of March 2025.
Several startups are offering technology infrastructure to cooperative banks and other financial institutions to support their digital transformation. These include core banking software, mobile banking applications, payment systems and compliance tools.
Another player, RUGR Fintech, raised $5 million in pre-Series A funding in September 2025, led by Vikasa India EIF I Fund, to expand its digital payments and rural banking infrastructure. title: EloElo Group raises $80 Mn in Series C led by Hornbill Capital, NBCUniversal
summary:
Bengaluru-based consumer AI and entertainment company EloElo Group has raised $80 million in a Series C funding round led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal. The round also saw participation from MIT Investment Co. and existing investors Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners and others.
The fresh capital will be used to fund original content across languages, support the international launch of its micro drama platform Story TV, and expand investments in Dolphin AI, its agentic AI creative suite.
Founded in 2020 by former Flipkart executive Saurabh Pandey, EloElo Group operates Story TV, a micro drama platform, alongside Master, a micro learning platform, Dolphin AI and Voxy AI, an AI companion agent. Story TV offers over 5,000 micro dramas across six languages, with a new drama launched every three hours. The platform records 95 minutes of daily time spent per user, according to the company.
The company owns the content, distribution and AI-powered production engine behind its entertainment business. Across its apps, EloElo Group has over 40 million monthly active users and has crossed 300 million installs.
The latest funding round takes the company's total capital raised to $130 million which includes a $13.5 million Series B round raised in April 2025.
EloElo said it achieved multi-fold revenue growth over the past year and has scaled with profitable unit economics. EloElo began monetising in May 2024 and reported revenue of Rs 69.5 crore in FY25, with losses remaining largely flat. Its FY26 results are yet to be filed.
Micro dramas are among the fastest-growing formats in global entertainment. According to Omdia, the industry is expected to generate $14 billion globally by the end of 2026. In India, Redseer estimates that 40 million people paid for a micro drama at least once in FY26, while Lumikai's State of India Interactive Media Report projects the market to reach $4.5 billion by 2030.
EloElo Group said it will also use the fresh capital to expand its content slate, with a focus on premium originals, and take its micro drama business to international markets, including the US.
EloElo Group’s Master competes with Seekho, which is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Lightspeed and raised $28 million in a Series B round last September. title: Bakingo's revenue crosses Rs 400 Cr in FY26, losses double
summary:
India's online bakery market has grown beyond traditional birthday cakes, with customised desserts, premium baked goods and quick delivery becoming an increasingly important part of the celebration and gifting economy. Bakingo has tapped into this demand to build a business generating over Rs 400 crore revenue in FY26. However, higher operating costs continued to weigh on its bottom line, with the company's losses doubling to Rs 37 crore during the last fiscal year.
Bakingo’s revenue from operations grew by 35% year-on-year to Rs 405.8 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 300.3 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies.

Founded in 2016 by Himanshu Chawla, Shrey Sehgal and Suman Patra, Bakingo operates an online bakery business offering a range of cakes and desserts, including cheesecakes, gourmet cakes and jar cakes. The company has a presence across 30-plus cities, supported by a network of over 100 kitchens and a catalogue of more than 100 products. Sales of these bakery products remained its sole source of revenue for the firm in FY26.
It also earned Rs 7.3 crore from interests on investments and fixed deposits, which pushed its overall income to Rs 413.65 crore in FY26.
For the bakery firm, raw material procurement for cakes and desserts remained its largest expense, accounting for over 43% of the total expenditure. This cost increased 40% year-on-year to Rs 194.45 crore in FY26 from Rs 138.7 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Employee benefit expenses also rose 40% to Rs 31.6 crore, while advertising expenses increased 35% to Rs 75.4 crore. Commission and platform fees surged over 39% to Rs 53 crore. Other overheads, including delivery and transportation, outsourced support, and power and fuel costs, further added to the expenditure.
Overall, Bakingo's total expenses increased 38.7% to Rs 450.5 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 324.7 crore in FY25.
Despite recording 35% revenue growth in FY26, Bakingo's bottom line remained under pressure as operating expenses grew at a faster pace, resulting in its losses more than doubling to Rs 36.9 crore in the fiscal year.

Its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at -39% and -7.48%, respectively. On a unit level, Bakingo spent Rs 1.11 to earn a single rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its total current assets stood at Rs 86 crore, including cash and bank balance of Rs 30 crore during the last fiscal year.
Bakingo has raised $26.5 million to date across two funding rounds. This includes a Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) funding round in August this year, led by existing investor Faering Capital at a valuation of $173 million, as exclusively reported by Entrackr.
When Theobroma was acquired for a valuation of close to Rs 2600 crore in FY 24-25, it was also clocking revenues in the same range as Bakingo in FY26. Perhaps it is those numbers that have driven the firm to invest strongly in advertising and growth, but the valuation gap is significant. The starkest of course is the brand itself, which occupies a distinctly massier segment than Theobroma. That will also make it tougher to deliver margins that can meet investor expectations. We really think there is a long haul ahead for Bakingo in a part of the market that has little by way of protection, and the firm needs to think long and hard about its next steps.

Managed workspace solutions provider IndiQube announced its Q2 FY27 financial results today, reporting a 35% year-on-year increase in operating revenue. The Bengaluru-based company’s net loss narrowed 80% to Rs 5.90 crore in the quarter ended September 2026.
IndiQube’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 472 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 350 crore in Q2 FY26, according to financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

In the first half of FY27, IndiQube’s revenue from operations grew 35.7% to Rs 895 crore from Rs 659.5 crore in the corresponding period of FY26.
Founded in 2015, IndiQube offers managed workspace solutions to startups, enterprises and SMEs across major Indian cities. The company also recorded Rs 20 crore in other income during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 492 crore compared to Rs 367 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
For the managed office provider, depreciation on leases remained its largest cost component, increasing 25% year-on-year to Rs 195 crore in Q2 FY27. Finance costs stood at Rs 129 crore, while employee benefit expenses declined marginally to Rs 24.5 crore.
Meanwhile, the cost of materials increased 11.5% to Rs 29 crore from Rs 26 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Overall, IndiQube’s total expenses increased 23.5% year-on-year to Rs 500 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 405 crore in Q2 FY26.
At the bottom line, the company narrowed its net loss by 80.3% to Rs 5.90 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 29.90 crore in the year-ago quarter.
On a sequential basis, revenue from operations grew 11.6% to Rs 472 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 423 crore in Q1 FY27. Meanwhile, the company’s net loss narrowed 74.8% to Rs 5.90 crore from Rs 23.40 crore during the same period.

title: Awfis reports Rs 439 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27; profit grows 93%
summary:
Co-working solutions provider Awfis announced its Q2 FY27 financial results on Tuesday, reporting a 20% year-on-year growth in operating revenue. The company’s net profit nearly doubled to Rs 30.8 crore during the quarter ended September 2026.
The Delhi-based company’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 439 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 367 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statements sourced from the NSE.


 
Other income contributed Rs 25.6 crore, taking Awfis’ total income to Rs 464.3 crore during the quarter.
For the first half of FY27, Awfis reported a 23% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 863.6 crore from Rs 701.6 crore in the corresponding period last year. 
Co-working spaces remained Awfis’ largest revenue contributor, accounting for over 83% of its operating revenue. Revenue from the segment grew 22% year-on-year to Rs 363.6 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 297.4 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Meanwhile, its construction and fit-out projects business contributed Rs 75.2 crore during the quarter.
On the expenditure front, depreciation on leases remained Awfis’ largest cost component, rising 25% year-on-year to Rs 119 crore. Subcontracting costs stood at Rs 59.7 crore, while employee benefit expenses remained flat at Rs 32.7 crore. Finance costs and other operating overheads took total expenses to Rs 433 crore in Q2 FY27, up from Rs 377 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
The strong revenue led Awfis to nearly double its profit to Rs 30.8 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 16 crore in the year-ago quarter. 
On a sequential basis, Awfis’ revenue from operations remained largely stable at Rs 438.7 crore compared to Rs 424.9 crore in Q1 FY27, while net profit increased 28% from Rs 24 crore in the previous quarter.
At the end of today’s trading session, Awfis’ stock closed at Rs 241.2, valuing the company at a market capitalization of Rs 1,726 crore (approximately $182 million).

summary:

The company plans to expand its retail network to over 1,000 outlets in the next three to five years, according to a press release.
GIVA also raised $28 million in debt in May this year, which could be part of the current round. Entrackr exclusively reported the development.
Founded in 2019 by Ishendra Agarwal, GIVA offers jewellery across sterling silver, gold and lab-grown diamonds. The company operates through its own retail stores, D2C website and third-party e-commerce and quick-commerce platforms.
GIVA currently operates over 400 stores across India and Sri Lanka, with a presence in Tier I and Tier II markets.
The company said it grew at a CAGR of over 70% in the past three years, ending FY26 with revenue of around Rs 865 crore. It will use the fresh capital to strengthen its leadership team, expand manufacturing capabilities and increase its offline presence.
The company has raised over $258 million to date, including Rs 110 crore (around $12 million) in a Series C extension round led by HPV CC1 Ltd in February this year.
While GIVA is yet to file its FY26 financials, its operating revenue grew 89% year-on-year to Rs 518 crore in FY25. Its losses increased 22% to Rs 72 crore during the same period.
GIVA competes with organised jewellery players such as BlueStone, CaratLane, Melorra, Candere and Tanishq, along with newer brands including Palmonas, Jewelbox, Limelight Lab Grown Diamonds, Fiona Diamonds and Firefly Diamonds.

title: Decoding: Spill Games’ Rs 100 Cr Series A round, valuation and cap table
summary:
Bengaluru-based mobile gaming startup Spill Games has raised around Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) in a Series A round led by Elevation Capital, with participation from existing investors Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital. Following the latest allotment, the company's co-founders collectively hold a 41.23% stake.
The latest round values Spill Games at around Rs 400 crore, marking a 3.5X jump from its seed valuation of Rs 115 crore in April 2026, when it raised around Rs 27 crore.
According to the company's regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, Spill Games has allotted 6,094 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 1,65,110 per share, along with 10 equity shares.
Elevation Capital invested Rs 80 crore in the round, while Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital infused Rs 12.6 crore and Rs 8 crore, respectively.
As per the filing, the fresh proceeds will be used to scale successful games, expand its portfolio, invest in user acquisition, strengthen its AI and technology capabilities, and selectively hire talent. The company monetises its games through advertising and in-app purchases.
Founded in 2024 by former PlaySimple Games executives Om Misra, Tapan Ranjan and Harsh Garg, Spill Games is building an AI-led mobile gaming studio focused on free-to-play casual, puzzle and hybrid-casual games for global audiences.


Following the latest allotment, Elevation Capital emerged as Spill Games' largest external shareholder with a 20% stake, followed by Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital with 11.78% and 8.93%, respectively. All In Capital and M-League Limited held 7.48% and 2.70%, respectively. CRED founder Kunal Shah also holds a 0.68% stake in the company.
The three co-founders collectively hold a 41.23% stake in Spill Games. Misra owns 14.02%, while Garg and Ranjan hold 13.61% each.

title: Snitch revenue grows 68% to Rs 835 Cr in FY26; posts Rs 27 Cr loss
summary:
India’s men’s fast-fashion market has shifted significantly over the past few years, with consumers becoming more experimental in their style choices and fashion preferences. Snitch is among the brands that have capitalised on this trend, growing its revenue 3.4X over the past two fiscal years while keeping its losses relatively contained.
Snitch’s revenue from operations grew 67.7% year-on-year to Rs 835 crore in FY26 from Rs 498 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Founded in 2020 by Siddharth Dungarwal, Snitch sells trendy men’s apparel and accessories through its website and app. Apparel and accessories remain the company’s sole revenue stream. It also earned Rs 14 crore in other income, largely through interest on deposits and long-term investments, taking its total income to Rs 849 crore in FY26.

The company has also entered the quick commerce segment as it looks to expand its reach and delivery capabilities. At the same time, Snitch has been expanding its offline presence. According to its website, the brand operates 142 stores across India, including in metro and Tier II cities.
For the D2C fashion brand, procurement of apparel and accessories remained the largest cost component, accounting for around 51% of its overall expenditure. In line with the growth in scale, this expense increased 92.2% to Rs 444 crore in FY26 from Rs 231 crore in FY25.
Snitch spent Rs 108 crore on advertising and marketing during the year, while employee benefit expenses increased to Rs 81 crore. Marketplace charges, rent, delivery and other overheads also added to the cost base. As a result, its total expenditure increased 71.9% to Rs 873 crore in FY26 from Rs 508 crore in FY25.
With expenses growing slightly faster than revenue, Snitch reported a net loss of Rs 27 crore in FY26. On a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.05 to earn a rupee in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at -8.6% and -3%, respectively.

Snitch has raised over $53 million to date, including a $40 million Series B round led by 360 ONE Asset in June 2025.
For a company that has scaled its revenue to Rs 835 crore in just a few years, keeping losses at Rs 27 crore is a relatively encouraging sign. While the business is yet to turn profitable, its growing scale, expanding offline presence and entry into quick commerce provide room for further growth. The bigger question now is whether Snitch can convert this scale into sustainable profits without letting its costs grow faster than revenue.
Snitch operates in an increasingly competitive D2C fashion market, competing with brands such as The Souled Store, Rare Rabbit and Wrogn. The Souled Store reported a 37% growth in revenue to Rs 492 crore in FY25, while premium fashion brand Rare Rabbit reported revenue of Rs 818 crore. Meanwhile, Wrogn, backed by Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail, reported revenue of Rs 244 crore in FY26.

title: Exclusive: Armatrix kicks off Rs 67 Cr seed round at 4.8X valuation premium
summary:
Deeptech robotics startup Armatrix has raised Rs 67.28 crore in a seed funding round led by UK-based Crane Venture Partners, along with participation from new and existing investors.
The fresh funding comes less than a year after its pre-seed round and values the company nearly 5X higher than its previous round.
In January 2026, Armatrix had raised $2.1 million in a pre-seed round led by pi Ventures, with participation from Inuka Capital, Boundless Ventures, Boost VC, Turbostart and gradCapital.
According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the company has allotted 4,070 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 1,64,900 per share, along with 10 equity shares, to raise the capital.
The funding round appears to be ongoing, with the Delhi-based company likely to raise more capital in subsequent tranches.
Crane Venture Partners led the round with an investment of Rs 40 crore. Existing investor pi Ventures infused Rs 15 crore, followed by gradCapital with Rs 4.52 crore, Boundless Ventures with Rs 2.5 crore and Inuka Capital with Rs 2.37 crore. NKSquared also joined the round with an investment of Rs 2.37 crore, marking its entry into the company.
Among other investors, AL Trust, Saurabh Chandra, Unacademy co-founder Roman Saini and existing investor Narayan Rangarajan collectively invested Rs 67 lakh in the round.
According to Entrackr's estimates, Armatrix's valuation jumped 4.8X to Rs 360 crore in the seed round from Rs 75 crore in its pre-seed round. The company plans to use the fresh proceeds for business expansion and general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2024 by Vishrant Dave, Prateesh Awasthi and Ayush Ranjan, Bengaluru-based Armatrix develops snake-like robotic manipulators for operations in hazardous and confined industrial spaces. Its technology is designed for inspection and maintenance across sectors such as shipbuilding, nuclear energy, oil and gas, and aviation, reducing the need for human workers to enter dangerous spaces.
According to Moneycontrol, Armatrix was in talks to raise $15 million in a seed round led by Crane Venture Partners.
The company remained at the pre-revenue stage in FY26 and reported a net loss of Rs 3.05 crore.

title: Solgram raises over $1 Mn in pre-seed round led by DSG Consumer Partners, Saama Capital
summary:
Gurugram-based premium grocery platform Solgram has raised over $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by DSG Consumer Partners and Saama Capital. Hospitality entrepreneur Kapil Chopra also participated in the round.
The funding comes within a quarter of the company's launch.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its cold-chain infrastructure, strengthen its technology stack, deepen sourcing relationships and scale operations across the National Capital Region (NCR), Solgram said in a press release.
Founded by Shashank Shekhar Sharma, Solgram operates a premium grocery platform focused on fresh produce, dairy, meats, seafood and other temperature-sensitive products. The company aims to maintain product quality through an end-to-end temperature-controlled supply chain.
Its operations cover sourcing, quality inspection, storage, fulfilment and delivery. The company operates temperature-controlled stores with dedicated zones for different product categories, along with sealed thermal packaging and dedicated last-mile infrastructure.
Solgram's assortment includes fresh produce, dairy, meats, seafood, bakery, gourmet pantry products and emerging food brands. It also offers Mindful Mode, a health-focused shopping category featuring products with cleaner labels, nutritional information and provenance details.
The platform offers scheduled batched delivery and express delivery options.
Currently operational in Gurugram, Solgram plans to expand across the NCR before entering other Tier-I cities in the coming months. The company said it intends to build operational density and consistency in individual clusters before expanding into new markets.

title: The Croffle Guys raises Rs 14 Cr from V3 Ventures, N.A.N Partners at Rs 100 Cr valuation

title: Vedantu revenue grows  17% to Rs 267 Cr in FY26; cuts losses before exceptional items
summary:
The online education space has been through a sharp shakeout over the past two-three years, with Byju’s collapse and Unacademy’s acquisition by UpGrad reshaping the competitive landscape. Against these odds, Vedantu managed to grow its revenue and improve its operating metrics in FY26. Its bottom line also improved, excluding the impact of exceptional items.
Bengaluru-based edtech unicorn’s revenue from operations grew 17.6% to Rs 267 crore in FY26 from Rs 227 crore in the previous fiscal, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
Tuition fees remained its largest revenue source for Vedantu, growing 16.8% to Rs 222 crore from Rs 190 crore in FY25. Revenue from books, uniforms and other products increased 31.8% to Rs 29 crore, while e-learning project income stood at Rs 6.3 crore during the last fiscal year.
With non-operating income of Rs 3.8 crore, the firm posted a total income of Rs 270 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026.

On the expense side, employee benefit expenses, the largest cost component, declined 12.8% to Rs 191 crore in FY26 from Rs 219.5 crore in FY25. It also includes Rs 7.2 crore as ESOP cost (non-cash. Contract and outsourced resources costs surged 54.3% to Rs 71 crore, while depreciation expenses declined 5.8% to Rs 65 crore.
Advertising and promotional expenses increased 7.4% to Rs 29 crore, whereas technology expenses stood at Rs 12 crore . Overall, Vedantu’s total expenses remained largely flat at Rs 442 crore in FY26.
With the decent growth coupled with stable expenses, Vedantu’s losses before exceptional items and tax decreased by 18.6% to Rs 171 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 210 crore in FY25.  
Note: We have excluded exceptional income and expenses arising from changes in the fair valuation of consideration payable (liability towards future obligations) in both FY25 and FY26 to present a clearer picture of the company's financial performance.
At the unit level, the company also improved its expense-to-operating revenue ratio. As of March 2026, the company had cash and bank balances of Rs 77.25 crore, while its total current assets stood at Rs 160 crore.
The improvement in pre-exceptional performance comes as Vedantu continues to compete in a more consolidated edtech market. Byju’s has collapsed, while Unacademy has scaled back its operations, leaving Physics Wallah as a key competitor in the online education and test-preparation space. Unlike the earlier funding-led expansion phase, the next phase of competition is likely to depend more on student outcomes, pricing and the ability to build a sustainable business.
Vedantu raised $11 million from internal investors in September 2025 as part of a larger round led by ABC World Asia, with participation from Accel India and Omidyar. The funding could support its efforts to strengthen its offerings and compete with Physics Wallah.
The improvement in Vedantu’s core performance suggests that the company may be entering a more stable phase after the difficult period faced by the edtech sector. Its ability to grow revenue while keeping overall expenses largely flat offers a positive sign. The focus now will be on sustaining this growth, improving cash flows and building a stronger business as competition grows.
The fact that PW is now a public firm probably is not the disadvantage it could be for Vedantu, as it can still chase opportunities without the glare of market appraisal hanging over it. Though some would say being public has made PW more disciplined. We believe Vedantu definitely has it in it to spring a surprise yet, which could come as early as the end of the ongoing financial year (FY27) or next year (FY28).

title: TBO Tek posts Rs 866 Cr revenue and Rs 76 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
summary:
Travel distribution platform TBO Tek announced its Q2 FY27 financial results today, reporting a 52.5% year-on-year growth in operating revenue. The Gurugram-based company also recorded a 12% increase in net profit to Rs 76 crore during the quarter ended September 2026.
TBO Tek’s operating revenue rose to Rs 865.6 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 567.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, according to its unaudited financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange.


 
The company’s total income stood at Rs 880.4 crore in Q2 FY27, including Rs 14.8 crore earned through non-operating income.
Hotel and package bookings continued to be TBO Tek’s largest revenue contributor, accounting for 86% of its total revenue. Income from this segment grew 55% year-on-year to Rs 745 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 479.4 crore in Q2 FY26. Air ticketing and other allied services contributed the remaining Rs 120 crore.
As hotels and packages remained the largest revenue source, the service fees associated with them became the company’s biggest cost center, accounting for 39% of the total expenditure at Rs 304.5 crore in Q2 FY27. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 190.7 crore during the quarter.
TBO Tek’s total expenses increased 55% year-on-year to Rs 780.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 504.4 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year. The company reported a 12.6% rise in net profit to Rs 76 crore during the quarter from Rs 67.5 crore in Q2 FY26.
At the end of Monday’s trading session, TBO Tek shares were trading at Rs 1,593.5 giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 17,303 crore.

title: DeHaat posts Rs 2,715 Cr revenue in FY26
summary:
Several agritech companies that initially started as marketplaces for selling agricultural inputs and outputs are now moving towards building their own brands. The shift is aimed at improving margins, gaining better control over pricing, and reducing dependence on third-party products.
Full-stack agritech platform DeHaat has pursued this strategy over the past few years by expanding its portfolio of in-house brands. The shift towards building its own brands appears to have involved a near-term trade-off on growth, with operating revenue declining nearly 10% in FY26, even as the company continued to reshape its business. The firm’s net loss also widened in FY26 as it continued to invest in its in-house brands
DeHaat's revenue from operations fell 9.8% to Rs 2,715 crore in FY26 from Rs 3,010 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
The sale of agricultural inputs, including seeds, fertilisers and other farm-related products, contributed Rs 517 crore, accounting for around 19% of its operating revenue. The remaining revenue came from its agricultural output business, which includes staples, chillies and consumer-facing initiatives such as Farm Plus and HonestFarms.
India continued to be DeHaat's largest market, contributing 83% of its total revenue. The remaining income came from international markets, including the UK, Europe, the Middle East, Thailand and Russia.

On the cost side, procurement of materials remained the firm's largest expense, accounting for nearly 80% of its overall expenditure. As business scale moderated, this cost also declined by 11.7% to Rs 2,390 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses fell 9.1% to Rs 159 crore in the same period.
Other expenses, including transportation, rent, warehousing, sales and branding, along with legal and administrative overheads, took the company's total expenditure to Rs 2,972 crore in FY26, against Rs 3,242 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Despite an 8.3% decline in overall expenses, the revenue fall put further pressure on the company's bottom line, resulting in DeHaat's losses increasing by 11.4% to Rs 224 crore in FY26 from Rs 201 crore in FY25.
Note: We have excluded the Rs 578 crore income recorded from the change in the fair value of preference shares to present a clearer picture of the company's financial performance.
At a unit level, DeHaat spent Rs 1.09 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -53.9%, while its EBITDA margin was recorded at 6%. The company also had current assets of around Rs 1,000 crore at the end of the fiscal year.
The agritech sector has been navigating a more measured growth phase since the funding boom of 2021-22, with startups placing greater emphasis on sustainable business models. DeHaat’s move beyond its original marketplace model and focus on building in-house brands could help it improve margins, strengthen customer relationships and gain greater control over its business. While the transition has affected near-term growth and profitability, it could open up new opportunities over time. The key question is how quickly DeHaat can scale these brands and translate them into a stronger growth and profitability engine.

title: Health-tech startup Clinics On Cloud raises $12.5 Mn in Series A round
summary:
Pune-based health-tech startup Clinics On Cloud has raised $12.5 million in a Series A funding round from Dubai-based investors through Model42, powered by Enlightened Minds Investments.
The fresh funds will be used to strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI)-led healthcare capabilities, expand research and development (R&D), and grow its connected microclinic network, Clinics On Cloud said in a press release.
The funding will also support the company’s international expansion, with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) serving as its global expansion hub. The company plans to explore opportunities across Africa, the United States and Southeast Asia.
Clinics On Cloud also plans to establish partnerships with healthcare providers, technology companies and organisations seeking to deploy connected microclinics across different markets.
Founded in 2018 by Abhay Agarwal, Clinics On Cloud develops technology-enabled healthcare infrastructure focused on preventive healthcare. The company has recorded over 3,500 deployments and conducted more than 12 million health screenings across eight countries.
Initially focused on Health ATMs, the company has expanded its portfolio to include Health Lounges, Box Clinics and Mobile Medical Units. Its solutions combine preventive health screening, AI-assisted health insights and telemedicine to enable hospitals, pharmacies, healthcare entrepreneurs, corporates and government organisations to establish microclinics across workplaces, housing societies, malls and underserved communities.
The company’s infrastructure has been deployed across government health centres, hospitals, corporate campuses and rural communities, as well as Indian defence establishments, including the Army, Navy and Border Security Force (BSF).
Clinics On Cloud also plans to collaborate with global healthcare innovators to integrate AI and advanced screening technologies into its platform.

summary:
Fitness platform OBSESS has raised approximately Rs 3 crore in an angel funding round from Centricity co-founder Pushpendra Singh, Amit Goel and Harshit Vij.

The Noida-based startup aims to address fragmentation in India's fitness and wellness industry, where gyms, trainers, sports facilities, nutrition experts and fitness brands often operate independently.
OBSESS offers a technology-driven marketplace that brings together sports venues, fitness centres, coaches, nutrition and wellness brands, and related services.

title: Antler India leads pre-seed round in last-mile delivery startup Dispatch Network
summary:
Pune-based last-mile delivery startup Dispatch Network has raised Rs 5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Antler India, with participation from angel investors Krishi Fagwani, founder of Thrive, Yashin Mahadevia and Parth Modwadhia.
The fresh capital will be used to expand the company's artificial intelligence (AI) team working on its proprietary Large Logistics Spatio-Temporal Model (LLSTM), a foundation AI model designed for intracity logistics and mobility, Dispatch Network said in a press release.
The startup plans to expand its operations to 50,000 orders per day across five cities.
Co-founded in 2023 by Rajit Arya and Navneeth Kannan, Dispatch operates a last-mile delivery network that uses AI to optimise order allocation, rider productivity and delivery routes.
The company's model sequences orders across multiple platforms, determining which order a rider should take next and where they should wait for subsequent deliveries.
According to the company, its network has processed over 100,000 deliveries since launching in June 2026. Monthly delivery volumes increased from 3,014 in June to 55,000 in October. The startup currently handles around 3,500 deliveries per day.
Dispatch said its model has reduced empty kilometres by two-thirds, while riders earn approximately 55% more per month compared to the industry average. The company also reported rider retention 80% higher than the industry average.
The startup currently serves food delivery and quick-commerce platforms, including Zomato, Swiggy, Zepto, Instamart and BigBasket. It also works with restaurants and stores through direct APIs and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC).
Following its launch in Pune, Dispatch plans to expand to Mumbai in November 2026.
Dispatch Network, operated by Artem Network Private Limited, entered the last-mile delivery segment in 2026 and went live in Pune in June. Arya has been working in electric mobility since 2009, while Kannan has a decade of experience in mobility systems as a product architect and engineer.

title: MobiKwik posts highest-ever quarterly PAT of Rs 11.8 Cr in Q2 FY27
summary:
Fintech platform MobiKwik announced its results for the second quarter of the financial year ending March 2027 (Q2 FY27). The company reported a year-on-year increase of over 9% in operating revenue and posted its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 11.8 crore.
MobiKwik's revenue from operations increased to Rs 295.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 270.2 crore in Q2 FY26, its unaudited financial statements accessed from the National Stock Exchange (NSE) show.

The company’s total income stood at Rs 302.7 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 279.3 crore a year earlier, including Rs 7 crore earned through non-operating income.
MobiKwik's key revenue contributors included commissions from recharges and loan servicing, along with income from payment gateway and technology platform services. However, the company did not disclose a segment-wise revenue breakup in its quarterly filing.
On a sequential basis, the company's operating revenue grew 5% from Rs 281.5 crore in Q1 FY27.
The company's platform gross merchandise value (GMV) increased 35% year-on-year to an all-time quarterly high of Rs 59,677 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 44,114 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Lending disbursals also grew 34% to Rs 1,082.6 crore from Rs 807.1 crore during the same period.
For the fintech firm, payment gateway charges remained MobiKwik's largest expense in Q2 FY27, accounting for over 42% of its total costs. Employee benefit expenses surged 59% to Rs 56.2 crore during the quarter.
The company also reported financial guarantee costs of Rs 28.3 crore, while legal, advertising and marketing, finance and other overheads contributed to its overall expenditure. MobiKwik's total expenses stood at Rs 290.9 crore in Q2 FY27, marginally lower than Rs 296 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Mobikwik reported its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 11.8 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to a loss of Rs 28.6 crore in the same quarter last year. On a sequential basis, its profit increased 55% from Rs 7.6 crore in Q1 FY27.
The Gurugram-based firm also reported its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA of Rs 22.7 crore, compared to an EBITDA loss of Rs 6.4 crore in Q2 FY26. This marked the company's fourth consecutive profitable quarter.
As of 1:38 PM, MobiKwik shares were trading over 4% higher at Rs 223.5 apiece, giving the company a market capitalization of around Rs 1,770 crore.

summary:
SaaS firm Capillary Technologies reported a 51.4% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in the second quarter of the ongoing fiscal year (Q2 FY27). The company also reported a profit of Rs 22 crore during the quarter, compared to a marginal profit in the same period last year.
The Bengaluru-based company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 271 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 179 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, according to its financial statements sourced from the NSE.
Founded in 2008 by Aneesh Reddy, Krishna Mehra, and Ajay Modani, Capillary Technologies offers cloud-based loyalty, CRM, and customer engagement solutions to more than 465 brands across 53 countries. Its clientele includes Tata Digital, Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail, and Abbott Laboratories.
The company primarily generates revenue from subscription services, which contributed 95% of its operating revenue during the quarter. Installation and campaign services accounted for the remaining revenue. It also reported Rs 6 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 277 crore in Q2 FY27.

On a sequential basis, the company's operating revenue grew 5.5% from Rs 257 crore in Q1 FY27.
Employee benefits remained its largest expense, increasing 57% year-on-year to Rs 134 crore. Software and server charges stood at Rs 42 crore, while professional and consultancy fees accounted for Rs 39 crore. Overall, Capillary's total expenses increased 44% to Rs 232 crore during the quarter.
On the bottom line, the company reported a profit of Rs 22 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 0.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company had reported a loss of Rs 9.5 crore in Q1 FY27.
For context, Capillary Technologies had reported a 42.6% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 256.6 crore in Q1 FY27. However, its bottom line was impacted by an exceptional loss of Rs 33.4 crore linked to a cyber-enabled banking fraud at its Czech Republic subsidiary.
Separately, the company's promoter entity, Capillary Technologies Pte Ltd, offloaded a 4.14% stake through a bulk deal on the BSE in August 2026. The promoter entity sold 32.92 lakh shares worth Rs 171.5 crore. Before the transaction, it held a 48.92% stake in the company.

title: Razorpay receives final IFSCA licence to expand cross-border money movement from GIFT City
summary:
Razorpay has received the final Payment Service Provider (PSP) licence from the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) to operate in GIFT City, Gujarat. The licence will allow the fintech company to facilitate cross-border money movement to and from India under a single regulatory framework.
The approval follows an in-principle clearance granted in April 2026. With the licence, Razorpay plans to support global investing, international collections, settlements and multi-currency transactions through its GIFT City-based infrastructure.
The company has already integrated with RBL Bank and ICICI Bank, while key investment platforms are expected to go live soon. Razorpay said the infrastructure will allow investment platforms to integrate once and offer global investing services to Indian residents in line with FEMA and GIFT City regulations.
The company aims to reduce integration timelines from several months to two to three weeks by bringing banking, compliance and remittance services under a unified infrastructure.
According to the company, Indian residents invested $2.65 billion in overseas stocks and debt in FY26, marking a 56% year-on-year increase. Razorpay is looking to address the infrastructure requirements arising from this growing demand.
The licence also expands Razorpay's cross-border capabilities to include foreign currency transfers and multi-currency accounts. The company plans to extend the infrastructure to other financial flows, including services for non-resident Indians (NRIs).
Founded in 2014 by Shashank Kumar and Harshil Mathur, Razorpay provides payment and business banking solutions to businesses across India.

title: Indian startup funding nosedives 47.5% to $678 Mn in October
summary:
Indian startups raised $678 million in October, a 47.5% month-on-month decline, as the absence of large funding rounds dragged overall investments. No startup secured a funding round of $100 million or more, while only Tessolve and Even Healthcare crossed the $50 million mark. Growth stage deals received a boost from rounds raised by Boldfit, DailyObjects, RapidCanvas and Nat Habit, while early stage funding saw moderate participation from Auxo AI, Cent, Mesa and Matiks.

The month saw no reported layoffs, while Jio Platforms made a high-profile stock market debut, followed by listings of Zetwerk and AceVector, the operator of Snapdeal. Merger and acquisition activity, however, remained limited to select sectors.
[Overview]
According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $678 million in funding during October. This amount included 20 growth and late-stage deals totalling $414.6 million, along with 79 early-stage deals worth $263 million. Additionally, there were 9 undisclosed deals during the period.
Y-o-Y and M-o-M trend
October 2026 saw a sharp decline in startup funding compared to the same month last year. Total funding fell 60.8% to $677.8 million from $1.73 billion in October 2025. On a month-on-month basis, funding declined 47.5% from $1.29 billion in September. February was the strongest month for funding in 2026, with startups raising around $2 billion, followed by June, which also recorded around $2 billion. October’s decline came amid a lack of larger deals, with no startup raising $100 million or more during the month.

[Top 10 growth-stage deals]
Growth and late-stage startups saw activity across sectors in October, led by semiconductor solutions provider Tessolve Semiconductor, which raised $75 million, followed by healthtech startup Even Healthcare with $50 million. Sports and fitness brand Boldfit secured $42 million, while lifestyle brand DailyObjects and enterprise AI startup RapidCanvas raised $35 million and $29 million, respectively. Advanced materials manufacturer Simplify raised $25 million, followed by robotics startup Origin with $20 million. Beauty and wellness brand Nat Habit and AI startups Simplismart and Live2.ai raised $15 million, $14 million and $14 million, respectively.

[Top 10 early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups saw funding across AI, healthtech, edtech and gaming in October, led by enterprise AI startup AuxoAI, which raised $20.7 million, followed by healthtech startup Cent with $15 million. Mesa School of Business and Confido Health secured $12.5 million each, while gaming startup Spill Games raised $10.5 million. AI video platform Clueso, quantum computing startup Quanfluence and social gaming platform Matiks received $10 million each. Nutrition brand Ace Blend raised $9.91 million, while edtech startup byteXL secured $9 million to expand its technology training programmes.

[Mergers and acquisitions]
Indian startups recorded five acquisitions in October across SaaS, healthtech, cybersecurity and FMCG. Freshworks acquired AI startup Robusta, while healthtech startup Cent acquired Medsee and cybersecurity firm Protectt.ai acquired AIShield. In the FMCG sector, Marico acquired Satya Nutraceuticals for $110 million. Meanwhile, Hoola Health acquired UpTodd, marking continued consolidation in the healthtech sector.

[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru led startup funding in October with $420 million across 52 deals, accounting for 61.97% of the total capital raised. Delhi-NCR followed with $110.26 million across 18 deals, while Mumbai startups raised $57.53 million across 11 deals. Hyderabad secured $41.22 million across five deals, followed by Bhubaneswar with $11.5 million from a single deal.
E-commerce startups led sector-wise funding with $182.69 million across 27 deals, followed by AI startups with $131.12 million across 22 deals. Healthtech companies raised $104.61 million across 13 deals, while semiconductor startups secured $75 million in a single deal. Manufacturers raised $36.67 million across four deals, rounding out the top five segments.
[Series-wise deals]
Series B startups led funding in October with $209.34 million across 10 deals, followed by Series A companies with $135.35 million across 17 deals. Seed-stage startups raised $80.41 million across 41 deals, while Series C companies secured $61.5 million across three deals. Pre-Series A startups raised $23.24 million across seven deals.

[Key hirings and departures]
October saw key leadership appointments across startups and investment firms, with Mayank Khanduja joining Bessemer Venture Partners as a partner and Manas Poddar taking charge as CBO at OTPless. Sanjeev Bikhchandani continued as MD and group CEO at Info Edge, while Kiran U joined Bellatrix Aerospace as CFO. Other notable appointments included Basant Dhawan as CMO at Shoonya by Finvasia, Medhavi Singh as India country head at Aleph and Kamaldeep Singh as CEO at Infost Energy. Meanwhile, Sanjeev Bikhchandani and Mithun Sacheti were among the key departures, from Info Edge and Nazara Technologies, respectively.
[Tends]
Zorit comeback: Zorit (formerly Bijnis) raised funding from investors including Sparoww Capital and Info Edge Capital, which had written off its entire investment in the startup in 2023.
Vama funding: Spiritual tech startup Vama raised funding from the Dainik Bhaskar family office, which could be among its first recorded startup investments.
Quick home services race: Snabbit recorded an NTV of Rs 72 crore in Q2 FY27, marginally ahead of Urban Company's InstaHelp at Rs 71 crore. Snabbit reported a burn of Rs 142 crore against InstaHelp's adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 174 crore, although the figures may not be directly comparable.
Burma Burma follows Subway India with IPO filing: Hunger Pangs, the operator of Burma Burma, filed its DRHP for an IPO comprising a fresh issue of up to Rs 600 crore, with no OFS. The filing follows that of Subway India operator EverBrands India in September.

[Conclusion]
October’s funding slowdown reflects a more selective investment environment, with investors prioritising stronger business fundamentals and clearer paths to profitability. Indian startups have raised nearly $11 billion so far in 2026. If funding averages $1 billion in each of the remaining two months, the annual total could cross the $13 billion recorded in 2023. Otherwise, 2026 could end with the lowest annual funding in three years. The coming months will determine whether the slowdown is temporary or signals a prolonged period of cautious investment.

title: iD Fresh Food nears Rs 900 Cr revenue in FY26; profit before exceptional items surges 3X
summary:
Ready-to-cook food is becoming a staple in Indian kitchens as consumers seek convenience without giving up home-cooked meals. iD Fresh Food has built its business around this growing preference, clocking nearly Rs 900 crore in revenue in FY26 while remaining profitable.
iD Fresh Food’s revenue from operations increased 27.7% year-on-year to Rs 870 crore in FY26 from Rs 681 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
The Bengaluru-based company manufactures ready-to-cook products such as idli and dosa batter and parathas. It also trades in food products, including curd, paneer, coffee, specialty batter and other food items.
iD Fresh operates manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Haryana and Ajman in the UAE. Manufactured products such as parathas and various batters contributed Rs 671 crore, accounting for 75% of its total operating income. The remaining income came from traded goods, including dairy products, chapatis, beverages, and frozen fruits.

The firm also earned Rs 8 crore in other income, primarily from interest on current investments, taking its total income to Rs 879 crore in FY26.
Raw material procurement remained the largest cost component, accounting for 49% of the company's total expenditure. This expense increased 18.3% to Rs 394 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses also rose 16% to Rs 168 crore.
The company spent Rs 70 crore on advertising in FY25. Other expenses, including legal, rent, freight, transportation and overheads, pushed its total expenditure up 20.5% to Rs 801 crore in FY26 from Rs 665 crore in FY25.
Despite the rise in costs, strong revenue growth helped iD Fresh improve its profit before tax and exceptional items to Rs 79 crore in FY26 from Rs 24 crore in FY25.
Note: The analysis excludes exceptional items worth Rs 713 crore, primarily related to changes in the fair valuation of preference shares and gains arising from the deconsolidation of a subsidiary. These accounting adjustments are excluded to provide a clearer picture of the company's business performance.
iD Fresh Food reported EBITDA of Rs 111 crore in FY26, while its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at 17.4% and 13%, respectively. Its total current assets stood at Rs 250 crore during the fiscal year.

iD Fresh Food has established itself as one of the early players in India's ready-to-cook food market, building a sizeable business around products that were once largely prepared at home. However, the opportunity also comes with challenges. The success of the category has attracted several competitors, putting pressure on pricing, margins and distribution. For iD Fresh, the next phase of growth will depend not just on expanding its product portfolio and reach but also on making its distribution more efficient and building stronger consumer loyalty.
The challenge for iD Fresh is no longer proving that Indians are willing to pay for convenience, but convincing them to choose its products over an expanding list of alternatives.

title: TVS retains EV two-wheeler lead in October; Ather grows 3%, Ola declines 10%
summary:
India’s electric two-wheeler market continued its growth momentum in October, with registrations increasing to 2,23,847 units from 2,08,705 units in September, with TVS Motor retaining its leadership, while Ather Energy posted marginal growth and Ola Electric saw a decline in registrations.
According to latest Vahan data, TVS Motor led the market with 60,429 registrations in October, accounting for a 27% market share. The company’s registrations increased 11.08% month on month from 54,403 units in September, further strengthening its lead over other manufacturers.
Bajaj Auto retained the second position with 49,067 registrations and a 21.92% market share. However, its registrations grew marginally by 0.67% compared to 48,742 units in the previous month.
Ather Energy ranked third with 31,796 registrations and a 14.2% market share. Its registrations rose 2.75% month on month. The company also turned profitable in Q2 FY27 as revenue surged 63% year on year to Rs 1,464 crore.
Following 27% growth in September, Hero MotoCorp continued its strong run in October, with registrations increasing 22.34% month on month to 29,901 units from 24,440 units. The company held a 13.36% share of the electric two-wheeler market during the month.
Ola Electric remained in fifth position with 12,096 registrations and a 5.4% market share. It was the only player among the top five to report a monthly decline, with registrations falling 10.12% from 13,458 units in September.
Greaves Electric Mobility followed with 10,838 registrations, a 16.3% month-on-month increase from 9,319 units in September. River Mobility also posted strong growth, with registrations climbing 20.3% to 6,796 units against 5,649 units in September.
BGauss recorded 5,554 registrations, a 10.55% month-on-month increase, while E-Sprinto Green Energy posted a 6.36% growth in registrations to 2,124 units.
Motovolt Mobility entered the top 10 electric two-wheeler manufacturers in October, with registrations jumping 168% to 1,702 units from 635 units in September. In contrast, Bounce dropped out of the top 10 after registrations declined 65% to 1,075 units from 3,069 units in the previous month.

title: UPI hits record 25.47 billion transactions in October, daily value crosses Rs 1 lakh crore
summary:
Unified Payments Interface (UPI) processed a record 25.47 billion transactions worth Rs 31.53 lakh crore in October 2026, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
The October transaction volume grew 5.8% month-on-month (M-o-M) from 24.07 billion transactions processed in September. Transaction value also increased 7.4% from Rs 29.37 lakh crore in September.
October's transaction volume rose 5.8% month-on-month, with the month having 31 days compared with 30 days in September. On a daily basis, UPI processed an average of 822 million transactions in October, a 2.5% increase from 802 million in September. The average daily transaction value also rose to Rs 1,01,707 crore from Rs 97,913 crore in September.
On a year-on-year basis, UPI transaction volume grew 23%, while transaction value increased 16% in October.
UPI crossed the 23 billion monthly transaction mark for the first time in May 2026 with 23.2 billion transactions worth Rs 29.90 lakh crore. It then processed 23.66 billion transactions in July, followed by a record 24.51 billion transactions in August. The monthly volume declined to 24.07 billion in September before reaching a new high in October.
PhonePe led the UPI market in September with a 45.6% share of transaction volume, followed by Google Pay at 32.2% and Paytm at 8.1%, according to NPCI data. The three apps together accounted for nearly 86% of transactions through listed UPI apps. The October app-wise breakdown has not been released yet.
Meanwhile, Paytm founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma said the company aims to capture one-third of the UPI consumer payments market. The target was outlined during Paytm's Q2 FY27 earnings call, where Sharma said consumer market share was a key priority for the company.
Last month, NPCI deferred the implementation of the merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions until after Diwali. The revised implementation date will be notified separately.
The decision was taken by the UPI and Services Steering Committee on October 13, keeping the festive season in mind. The framework was originally scheduled to take effect from October 15.
The MDR framework provides for a 0.4% charge on specified person-to-merchant transactions above Rs 2,000, with a cap of Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. UPI payments of Rs 2,000 or less and person-to-person transactions will remain outside the levy.

title: Boba Bhai revenue and losses jump over two-fold in FY26
summary:
Bengaluru-based tea and beverage chain Boba Bhai more than doubled its revenue in the fiscal year ending March 2026, but its losses also widened as the Titan Capital-backed company expanded its operations and opened several dozen new stores.
The company’s revenue from operations spiked 139% to Rs 68 crore in FY26 from Rs 28.44 crore in the previous fiscal (FY25), according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.


Food and beverage sales, the primary source of revenue, surged 137.1% to Rs 67.26 crore in FY26, accounting for 99% of the company’s operating revenue. Revenue from scrap sales also increased to Rs 28 lakh from Rs 7 lakh in the previous fiscal year. 

Additionally, the company reported Rs 1 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 69 crore in FY26 from Rs 29.44 crore in FY25.

When it comes to costs, Boba Bhai’s cost of materials consumed, the largest expense head, surged 138.5% to Rs 25 crore in FY26, while employee benefit expenses increased 210.3% to Rs 13.5 crore. Advertising and promotional expenses also jumped 139.9% to Rs 13 crore, whereas commission expenses surged 155.9% to Rs 11.44 crore.
Other expenses, which accounted for 35% of the total expenditure, increased 120.3% to Rs 31.46 crore in FY26 Overall, Boba Bhai’s total expenses jumped 2.3X to Rs 90.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 39 crore in the previous fiscal year. Importantly, the company reported 188 employees at the end of  March 2026.
Despite the strong growth in operating revenue, Boba Bhai’s losses widened 2.2X to Rs 21.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 9.96 crore in FY25. However, its operating efficiency improved marginally, with expenses incurred to generate every rupee of operating revenue declining to Rs 1.33 from Rs 1.37 in the previous fiscal year.


Its EBITDA margin improved to -30.35% from -34.67%, while ROCE deteriorated to -41.12% from -32.47%. Meanwhile, cash and bank balances declined sharply to Rs 2.85 crore from Rs 24.07 crore.

Boba Bhai raised Rs 40 crore in March 2026 as it continued to expand its store network. The company currently operates around 100 stores across eight cities and plans to expand to 10 cities in FY27, while adding another 150-200 stores by the end of the fiscal.
The company’s next phase will test whether its expansion can translate into better unit economics. With employee, marketing and material costs rising alongside revenue, Boba Bhai will need to improve store-level profitability and cash generation as it scales.

Income from renting electric vehicles, its largest revenue stream, increased 30.3% to Rs 262 crore from Rs 201 crore and accounted for more than 93% of operating revenue during the fiscal year ending March 2026.
Revenue from the sale of goods declined 59.3% to Rs 9.2 crore while manpower services fell 57% to Rs 5.7 crore from Rs 13.2 crore. In contrast, delivery services revenue rose more than 22X to Rs 2.6 crore. Franchisee income increased 122.2% to Rs 80 lakh from Rs 36 lakh.
Yulu’s employee benefit expenses, its largest cost head, increased 6.8% to Rs 94 crore in FY26 from Rs 88 crore in FY25. Battery-as-a-service costs rose 3.6% to Rs 87 crore, while depreciation expenses declined marginally by 1.5% to Rs 65 crore. Finance costs surged 40.9% to Rs 15.5 crore, whereas the cost of materials consumed fell 60% to Rs 8 crore. Technology and infrastructure expenses increased 11.6% to Rs 15 crore.
Other expenses climbed 34.9% to Rs 92.5 crore from Rs 68.56 crore in FY25. Overall, Yulu’s total expenses increased 7.4% to Rs 377 crore in FY26 from Rs 351 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Bengaluru-based Yulu’s losses narrowed 23% to Rs 97 crore in FY26 from Rs 126 crore in FY25. The company also improved its operating efficiency, with expenses incurred to generate every rupee of operating revenue declining to Rs 1.34 from Rs 1.48 in the previous fiscal year. 


The company’s EBITDA margin improved to -5.89% in FY26 from -15.41% in FY25, while its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -119.29% compared with -27.26% a year earlier. Meanwhile, Yulu’s cash and bank balance increased to Rs 11.51 crore from Rs 9.65 crore, while total current assets rose to Rs 152 crore from Rs 102 crore.

The financial performance comes as Yulu looks to expand its electric two-wheeler rental network. The company raised $93 million in August 2026 and currently operates a fleet of around 50,000 vehicles. It plans to expand to about 20 cities over the next year and increase its fleet to 200,000 electric vehicles by 2028.
The expansion will require Yulu to scale its fleet and supporting infrastructure, including battery services, while managing the costs associated with operating a larger network.
The deeper push into B2B services is clearly a more attractive and convincing proposition from the firm, which investors have backed despite the poor start with its original consumer rental model in 2017. The losses, expansion plans and rising competition indicate more funding rounds will be needed, which makes the choice of cities and cost control key to success.
Gig workers power the revenue numbers so far, and there remains a strong case to look at other high usage categories to expand the market. While the journey so far has practically seen the market direct Yulu to what actually works, the next stage of the firm's growth puts the onus squarely on the founders to get it right.

[Financial results this week]

▪️ Air India and SBI card to launch co-branded credit card soon
Air India, India’s leading global airline, and SBI Card, the country’s largest pure-play credit card issuer, have announced a partnership to develop a new Visa-powered co-branded credit card programme. Anjali Sardana, founder of instant household services startup Pronto, has launched Provision Labs, a US-based physical AI venture focused on collecting real-world data to train and test AI systems for robotics and other applications. According to its website, the venture is backed by Lachy Groom, Glade Brook, General Catalyst and Bain Capital Ventures, all of whom have also invested in Pronto. Hygge Energy, which operates a peer-to-peer rooftop solar trading marketplace in Bengaluru, will extend its platform to connect customers with solar providers and financing options across India.

summary:
Logistics company Delhivery reported a 19.8% year-on-year growth in revenue in the second quarter of the ongoing fiscal year (Q2 FY27) and remained profitable during the period.
Delhivery’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 3,066 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,559 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).


The company primarily generates revenue from its logistics services, including freight handling, transportation and warehousing. It also recorded other income of Rs 67 crore, taking its total income to Rs 3,133 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,652 crore in Q2 FY26.
Freight, handling and servicing costs remained Delhivery’s largest expense, accounting for 70.97% of its total expenses. This cost increased 19.1% to Rs 2,195 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,843 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Employee benefit expenses increased 4.7% to Rs 446 crore from Rs 426 crore, while depreciation rose 11% to Rs 197.5 crore from Rs 178 crore. Finance costs declined 12.8% to Rs 34 crore, whereas other expenses remained largely flat at Rs 220 crore in Q2 FY27.
Overall, the company’s total expenses rose 14.2% to Rs 3,093 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,708 crore in Q2 FY26.
Delhivery posted a net profit of Rs 40.64 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with a net loss of Rs 50.50 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company had also posted a profit of Rs 32 crore in the first quarter of the ongoing fiscal year (Q1 FY27).
On a half-yearly basis, Delhivery’s operating revenue grew 23.6% to Rs 5,997 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 4,853 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit increased 78.9% to Rs 72.55 crore from Rs 40.55 crore during the same period.
Delhivery’s shares closed at Rs 386 apiece on Friday, taking the company’s market capitalisation to Rs 29,831 crore.

summary:
PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, reported a strong financial performance in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue registering a healthy year-on-year growth alongside a 43% increase in net profit compared to the corresponding quarter last year.

The company’s revenue from operations grew 35% to Rs 2,178 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,614 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the stock exchanges.


In terms of revenue composition, insurance broker services contributed Rs 2,015.19 crore to the company’s revenue, up 41.1% year on year from Rs 1,428.16 crore. Revenue from other services declined 12.3% to Rs 162.52 crore from Rs 185.39 crore.
On the expense front, Employee benefits, the company’s largest expense, increased 28.8% to Rs 773 crore. Advertising expenses surged 59.5% to Rs 447 crore, while network and internet costs jumped 65.1% to Rs 70.75 crore. Depreciation and amortisation stood at Rs 43.78 crore.

Other expenses rose 21.8% to Rs 733 crore. Consequently, the company’s total expenses increased 32.6% to Rs 2,067.66 crore in Q2 FY27.
The Gurugram-based company’s net profit stood at Rs 193 crore, compared to Rs 135 crore in Q2 FY26. 

For the first half of FY27, the company’s revenue from operations increased 37.3% to Rs 4,066 crore, compared with Rs 2,962 crore in the corresponding period last year. Its profit after tax surged 61.4% to Rs 355 crore from Rs 220 crore in the same period.

Since the end of Q1 FY27, PB Fintech’s share price has declined 38.3% to Rs 1,000 from Rs 1,620. Its market capitalisation also fell 37.2% to Rs 47,104 crore from Rs 74,957 crore during the same period.

title: Atomberg gets SEBI nod for proposed IPO
summary:
Consumer appliances maker Atomberg Technologies has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 450 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 7.65 crore shares by existing shareholders. The company is yet to announce the price band and timeline for the issue.
Atomberg plans to use Rs 90 crore from the fresh issue proceeds to repay or prepay its borrowings. It will allocate Rs 150 crore towards brand awareness and performance marketing activities, while another Rs 100 crore will be used for research and development (R&D). The remaining amount will go towards general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2012 by Manoj Meena, who was joined by Sibabrata Das as co-founder in 2013, Atomberg initially focused on energy-efficient ceiling fans. It has since expanded its portfolio to include mixer grinders, water purifiers, cold-pressed juicers and other consumer appliances.
Apart from its consumer appliance business, the company also manufactures and supplies proprietary motors, controllers and other components to enterprise customers such as Voltas, Godrej and Blue Star through its subsidiary, Atomberg Innovations.
On the financial front, Atomberg's revenue from operations increased 34.8% to Rs 1,293.77 crore in FY26 from Rs 959.51 crore in FY25. However, its adjusted EBITDA declined to Rs 37.12 crore during the fiscal year from Rs 51.35 crore in FY25. The company reported a loss of Rs 148.88 crore in FY26, narrowing from Rs 199.08 crore in FY24.
Atomberg has also seen partial exits by existing investors ahead of its proposed listing. A91 Partners, which has backed the company since 2019, has sold shares worth around Rs 445 crore while retaining a 21% stake, according to the company's IPO disclosures.
ICICI Securities, Avendus Capital and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

Founded in 2019, Traya focuses on addressing hair loss by identifying its root causes and provides personalised hair treatment plans supported by consultations with hair coaches and licensed physicians.
The sale of customised hair care kits was Traya's sole source of operating revenue. The company also earned Rs 8 crore through gains from the sale of investments, pushing its total income to Rs 593 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026 from Rs 343 crore in FY25.
On the cost side, advertising remained the largest expense, accounting for around 44% of the firm's total expenditure. Advertising costs nearly doubled to Rs 275 crore in FY26. Meanwhile, the cost of materials procured increased 68.7% to Rs 140 crore during the last fiscal year.
Traya spent Rs 81 crore on employee benefits in FY26. Its legal, transportation, technology and other overheads also catalyzed its total expenditure up 70.2% to Rs 623 crore in FY26 from Rs 366 crore in FY25.
Despite a 72.6% growth in operating revenue, the increase in expenses continued to weigh on the company's bottom line. Traya reported a net loss of Rs 29 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 23.5 crore in FY25.
At a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.06 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at -44.7% and -6.19%, respectively. The company had total current assets of Rs 174 crore as of March 2026.
Traya has raised approximately Rs 96 crore in funding to date. This includes a Rs 75 crore investment from Xponentia Capital in April 2024. Its backers include Fireside Ventures, Kae Capital and Whiteboard Capital. The firm is reportedly in talks to raise another Rs 300 crore from Verlinvest.
Hair thinning and hair loss are real concerns, particularly among India's youth. Factors such as water quality, nutritional deficiencies, eating habits, and poor sleep can all contribute to the problem. This has created an opportunity for startups to build businesses around hair care, with several brands now selling gummies, serums and supplements. Traya has managed to carve out a place in this growing market with its personalised treatment approach. It will be interesting to see how large this business can become and how soon the company can turn profitable.

title: Smartworks posts Rs 591 Cr revenue and Rs 26 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
summary:
Managed office space provider Smartworks reported its financial results for the quarter ended September 2026 (Q2 FY27). The company posted a 39% year-on-year growth in revenue during the period. Meanwhile, its EBITDA grew 37% to Rs 391 crore.
Smartworks’ revenue from operations rose to Rs 591 crore in the Q2 FY27 from Rs 425 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Smartworks derives the bulk of its operating revenue from the development, design and licensing of serviced office spaces, along with fit-out services and other ancillary offerings. The company also reported Rs 14 crore in non-operating income during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 605 crore in Q2 FY27.
On a sequential basis, the firm’s operating revenue grew 8% from Rs 546 crore in Q1 FY27.
On the cost side, depreciation related to lease expenses was the largest expense for Smartworks at Rs 259 crore, up 31% from Rs 198 crore in Q2 FY26. This was followed by operating expenses, which stood at Rs 172 crore during the quarter. Employee benefits expenses amounted to Rs 28 crore. Finance costs and other overheads took the company’s total expenditure to Rs 570 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 445 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
At the bottom line, Smartworks continued its profitability on a quarter-on-quarter basis and turned profitable on a year-on-year basis, reporting a net profit of Rs 26 crore in Q2 FY27 compared to a net loss of Rs 3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Meanwhile its EBITDA grew 37% year-on-year to Rs 391 crore during the quarter, with an EBITDA margin of over 66%.
For H1 FY27, Smartworks’ operating revenue grew 42% year-on-year to Rs 1,138 crore. The company also reported a net profit of Rs 39 crore, compared to a loss of Rs 7.3 crore in H1 FY26.

title: Starbucks India brews Rs 1,367 Cr revenue in FY26; cuts losses by 27%
summary:
Tata Starbucks, the 50:50 joint venture between Tata Consumer Products and Starbucks Corporation, has established itself as one of India’s largest coffee chains by revenue and store count. While the company has grown over the years, its bottom line remains in the red.
Starbucks’ revenue from operations grew a modest 7% year-on-year to Rs 1,367 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,277 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Incorporated in September 2011, the company operates cafes across India under the Starbucks brand. By 2025, Tata Starbucks had expanded to over 390 stores across 54 Indian cities, with approximately 4,300 partners (employees). Importantly, the company aims to expand its network to around 1,000 stores by 2028.
The sale of coffee and related products accounted for most of its revenue. The remaining income came from its loyalty programme, My Starbucks Rewards, through which customers earn loyalty points called Stars.
The procurement of coffee beans and other related products accounted for 24% of the company’s total expenditure. This cost increased 6% to Rs 356 crore in FY26 from Rs 336 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses also rose 9.8% to Rs 225 crore during the same period.
Rent, electricity, advertising, freight and other overheads took total expenses up 4.7% to Rs 1,514 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,446 crore in FY25.
With controlled spending, Starbucks narrowed its net loss by 27% to Rs 99 crore in FY26 from Rs 136 crore in FY25. However, its EBITDA stood at Rs 234 crore during the year.
At a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.11 to earn every rupee of operating revenue. On a standalone basis, its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -2.6%, while its EBITDA margin was 17%.
Its closest competitor, Café Coffee Day, reported revenue of Rs 1,094 crore and a net profit of Rs 14 crore. Starbucks also competes with several newer coffee brands, including Blue Tokai, Rage Coffee, Third Wave Coffee Roasters, Slay Coffee, Sleepy Owl and Seven Beans Co.
As newer coffee brands build their own loyal customer base, competition in India’s coffee market is getting stronger. For Starbucks, the challenge is not just to expand its store network but to get customers to keep coming back for its premium offerings. The question is whether India’s appetite for expensive coffee is deep enough to support its ambitious expansion plans while bringing its bottom line into the black. For Starbucks, a business that looks unlikely to hit the $200 million mark by 2030  raises its own issues of attention and perhaps, even relevance, if profits remain elusive.
